title: Output contract of an EOF audit lot
description: Strict format for multi-agent lot output files. Any lot (agent, script, human) producing EOF verdicts must respect this contract. The merge script refuses any non-conforming file instead of merging it.

lot_id.description: Unique identifier of the lot (ex: 'lot-mesures-har', 'lot-qcm-client', 'lot-osint-accessibilite'). Used to trace the origin of each verdict in the final report.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the file generation (ex: '2026-09-04T12:34:56+00:00'). Allows detecting stale outputs.

inputs.description: List of file paths or public URLs actually read by the lot. May be empty for a declarative lot (hand-filled QCM). Traceability: links a verdict to its data sources.

measurement.description: Optional. Measurement-state convention (cf. documentation/implementation/measurement-state-convention.md): reports a failure of the lot's SOURCE itself (ex. questionnaire file absent or unreadable), distinct from a failure on an individual criterion.

target.description: What was being looked for: file path, URL, field name.

detail.description: Short sentence, or null if status is 'ok' and there is nothing to add.

criteria.description: List of the criteria judged by this lot. A criterion may be partially filled in (context only) or fully settled (answer + coefficient). The merge script consolidates these multiple entries into a single verdict per criterion.

id.description: Identifier of the criterion in the EOF reference (ex: '1.5', '3.3') or in the quick diagnostic (ex: '0.1', '0.16'). Must exist in the reference, otherwise rejected.

answer.description: Exact label of the ticked option, from the reference vocabulary FOR THIS CRITERION (evaluation_options or screens depending on the type). If null, the criterion stays unsettled (contextual hint only).

coefficient.description: Numeric coefficient associated with the answer, according to the reference's evaluation_coefficient_options mapping. Must be null if and only if answer is null. If answer is non-null, it must be EXACTLY the coefficient defined by the reference for this label.

provenance.description: Provenance of the verdict or of the hint: 'collected' (measured by our scripts: HAR, HTTP headers, API), 'estimated' (deduced by an LLM from real evidence), 'declared' (publicly declared by the audited organization: accessibility page, legal notices), 'stated' (ticked by the client in the questionnaire, without proof), 'assumed' (deduced from a weak signal, ambiguous). Required if answer or context is non-null. Determines the merge precedence: collected > estimated > stated > declared > assumed (revised 2026-09-11: the client knows their technical reality directly, more reliable than a public declaration that is sometimes generic or dated).

source.description: Origin of the verdict or of the hint: file path (ex: 'audit/har-analysis.json'), public URL (ex: 'https://example.com/accessibilite'), or QCM line reference (ex: 'QCM question 3'). Required if answer or context is non-null. Non-empty string.

context.description: Contextual hint sentence, when the criterion is not settled but a signal exists. Displayed in the report appendix to help the human judgment. Never replaces a verdict: if the signal is ambiguous, leave answer null.

category.description: Type of data used to judge this criterion: 'automatable' (verdict settled by measurement or deterministic rule), 'partial' (weak hint, context only), 'no_data' (no data available for this criterion in this lot). Imposed vocabulary, inherited from the EOF mapping table.

not_applicable.description: Indicates whether the criterion is out of scope for this audited service: true removes the criterion from BOTH the numerator AND the denameinator of the optimization-potential calculation. Distinct from the answer '🚫 Not applicable', which leaves the max_potential in the denameinator.
